style: instrumental video game game-over theme, seamless 60 second loop. The final journal page of a startup survival game: the company died, the cause is stamped in red, and the player reads how it happened — then runs it back. Mood: bittersweet, wry, tender; sad and funny at the same time, a eulogy that cannot keep a straight face. A tender solo felt piano plays a slow, slightly clumsy reading of a simple melody — two notes land charmingly wrong and correct themselves; a small glockenspiel answers like a consolation; warm long upright bass notes underneath; the faintest brushed drums barely enter halfway. Harmony drifts from D minor to F major at the turnaround so the loop always ends warm, consoling, almost smiling — never tragic, never melodramatic. Intimate, dry, close-miked small-room production, humanized rubato edges but the loop still closes cleanly on the bar. 96 BPM, half-time feel. No vocals, no strings, no choir, no big swells, no intro, no outro, no fade-out.
